swd-debug-port-nrst-on-the-header.note: Re-read ST p65 (s6.3.15 + Table 49), p66 (Figure 21), p27 (Table 10 RST legend; Table 11 NRST = TSSOP20 pin 4, 'Device reset input / internal reset output (active low)'), p32 (note 7) and Infineon p29 Figure 20. Every number is on the page as written: permanent pull-up RPU 25/40/55 kOhm, VF(NRST) filtered pulse max 100 ns, VNF(NRST) not-filtered min 300 ns for 2.7<VDD<3.6 and 500 ns for 2.4<VDD<3.6, VIL(NRST) max 0.3 VDD+0.07, Vhys 200 mV typ. Figure 21 notes 1 and 2 are quoted verbatim and it does show 0.1 uF at the pin; Figure 20 does put nRESET on position 10. Envelope 2.7-3.6 V is exactly the band Table 49 attaches to the 300 ns row and envelope_note names the 2.4-2.7 V / 500 ns case correctly. No ESD ruling smuggled in.

swd-debug-port-termination-follows-silic.note: Re-read Infineon p29 s9.4 and p30 Table 5 + the paragraph under it, plus ST p32 note 7. The s9.4 sentences are quoted verbatim, including 'each external signal termination must be in the same direction as it is done in the device implementation'. Table 5 does give pull-down to GND on TCK/SWCLK and 10k-100k pull-up to VDDIO on TMS/SWDIO, TDI and nTRST with an MCU-implementation column, and the 'possible voltage divider in the debug clock signal' caution is on p30 as quoted. Level principle with no envelope is right: the rule is supply, clock and connector independent. One imprecision that does not touch the rule: the p30 citation note reads the required-termination column as giving 'none on TDO/SWO', but that column requires a 10k-100k pull-up on TDO - 'None. Termination, push-pull driver implemented' is the MCU-implementation cell.

swd-debug-port-unkeyed-header-pin-order.note: Re-read Infineon p29 (Figure 20 and its two notes) and p31 (Figure 23 and its notes), plus ST p31 PA13/PA14 rows. Figure 20's assignment matches the record cell for cell (1 VTref, 2 SWDIO/TMS, 3 GND, 4 SWCLK/TCK, 5 GND, 6 (SWO)/TDO, 7 (KEY) GND, 8 NC/TDI, 9 (GNDDetect) GND, 10 nRESET; 4 of 10 positions GND) and note 2 is verbatim. The prose does label the i -> (n+1)-i reversal geometry a DERIVATION that no cited source states, and it does NOT assert a reversed plug is safe: it says safety turns on the probe's rail pin being a sense input, which no cited page states - correct, Figure 23 note 2 only sets a supply-level contract, nothing about the pin's direction or impedance. Figure 23 does show VTref out of the I/O power domain to pin 1 with C7 = 100 nF. Two caveats, neither fatal: 'shrouded' is the record's word (Infineon note 1 says only a 10-way connector with 1.27-mm pitch, e.g. FTSH-105-01-L-DV-K), and the return-path class rests on an observation (4 of 10 GND, and SWDIO's nearest GND is diagonal, not beside it) rather than a rule - at level principle it cannot close the checklist's return-path row in any case.

swd-debug-port-edge-rate-sets-layout-dem.note: Re-read ST p64 (Table 48) cell by cell, TI p6 and p9, Infineon p30. Both original objections are cleared ON THE PAGE. (1) Min claim now exact: x0, 01, 11 and the Fm+ configuration block ALL show Min '-' on every fmax/tf/tr row, and the last row tEXTIpw (pulse width of external signals detected by the EXTI controller) is the only populated Min cell at 10 ns - so 'no fmax, tr or tf row carries a Min, the only Min is tEXTIpw = 10 ns' is true as written in all three places it appears (prose, p64 citation note, envelope_note). (2) No post-reset state is asserted anywhere: the rule key is slowest_setting_edge_ns and the prose says 'Read those as ENCODINGS, not as a reset state'. 125 ns IS the slowest row of the whole table - x0 125, 01 25, 11 5/8/12, Fm+ tf 12 / tr 34 - so the field name is earned, and 5 ns is still the fastest specified edge. Footnote 1 (OSPEEDRx[1:0], refer to RM0360 for the GPIO port configuration register) and footnote 2 (guaranteed by design, not tested in production) are as quoted, and no row is marked default. All conditions match: 125 ns at CL 50 pF VDDIOx>=2.4 V with fmax 2 MHz; 25 ns at fmax 10 MHz; 5/8/12 ns at CL 30 pF VDDIOx>=2.7, CL 50 pF VDDIOx>=2.7, CL 50 pF 2.4<=VDDIOx<2.7 with fmax 50/30/20 MHz. TI p6 verbatim: 'if a signal with a rise time long enough to encompass the time delay of the line is used (tr >> tau)', 'Figure 11 shows that C(dv/dt) = i only when the rise time is greater than the time delay of the line', 'the line is essentially resistive, so VIN/IIN = R0 = Z0', and the 20 mA identical for 150-3750 ft. TI p9 eq 40 / 43 / 44 exact, tau = l x delta is the ONE-WAY delay as the criterion says. Infineon p30 series-resistor paragraph and Figure 22 R16 = 20R in the SWCLK_TCK line only are verbatim.

swd-debug-port-stm32f0-internal-pulls.note: Re-read ST p32, p31, p61, p60, p43, p27, p65 and Infineon p30 from scratch. The series claim is GONE: the rule dict now holds only enforced_by, external_pull_required, swdio_internal, swclk_internal, nrst_internal and pull_kohm_min/typ/max - no external_series_required key - and grep finds no 'or series resistor' phrase; the only 'series' mentions are Table 46 footnote 4's own wording, the explicit hand-off, and the disclosure in the Infineon note. The hand-off contradicts nothing on its own pages: it declines to rule rather than denying Infineon, and the p30 citation note openly flags that the same page's series recommendation is deliberately not carried. The two NEW citations are load-bearing and both hold verbatim. p60 s6.3.14 opens: 'Unless otherwise specified, the parameters given in Table 46 are derived from tests performed under the conditions summarized in Table 21: General operating conditions.' - exactly the link the record claims. p43 Table 21 gives VDD 'Standard operating voltage' Min 2.4 Max 3.6 V on its own row (fHCLK and fPCLK 0-48 MHz above it), so the vio_v envelope matches the right row, not a neighbour; Table 21 continued on p44 adds no VDDIOx row, so VDD is the I/O supply for this part. Pull directions and values re-derived independently, nothing swapped: p32 note 7 verbatim 'After reset, these pins are configured as SWDIO and SWCLK alternate functions, and the internal pull-up on SWDIO pin and internal pull-down on SWCLK pin are activated'; p31 PA13 (SWDIO) TSSOP20 pin 19 and PA14 (SWCLK) TSSOP20 pin 20, both FT, both carrying note 7; p61 Table 46 RPU (VIN = VSS) and RPD (VIN = VDDIOx) both 25/40/55 kOhm with footnote 4's true-resistance-plus-switchable-PMOS/NMOS ~10 percent and CIO typ 5 pF; p27 Table 10 'RST - Bidirectional reset pin with embedded weak pull-up resistor' plus the all-I/Os-floating-after-reset note; p65 s6.3.15 'It is connected to a permanent pull-up resistor, RPU' with Table 49 RPU 25/40/55 kOhm - and p65's own preamble also defers to Table 21, so the envelope covers NRST too. Infineon p30 Table 5 gives pull-down to GND on TCK/SWCLK and 10k-100k pull-up to VDDIO on TMS/SWDIO, and the record reads that column correctly as 'where the MCU does not implement them'.
